before: iCloud, Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook, synced two ways and colour-coded in a single view. Toggle any calendar off when you don’t want to see it — the rest keeps working.
after: View selected iCloud and Google calendars together; Premium adds Microsoft calendars. Edit where your account permissions allow, and check the source calendar after changes.

before: Grab an event and slide it to a new time or a different day. Pull its top or bottom edge to change how long it runs. No modal, no save button.
after: Move editable events to another time or day, or resize them in the timeline. For a repeating event, choose which occurrences to change and review the saved result.

before: That is the main way to edit. Drag an event to another time or another day, or pull its top or bottom edge to change the duration. Changes sync straight back to the source calendar.
after: You can move editable events and resize them in the timeline. Check the recurrence choice and saved time; connected-calendar updates depend on permissions and successful synchronization.

before: The same events, arranged for the question you are actually asking — and every one of them carrying the forecast.
after: Choose an overview or a detailed timeline, with available weather alongside supported views.

before: An hourly grid where every row carries its own forecast. You see the 3pm meeting and the 3pm rain in the same glance — no second app, no guessing.
after: Compare appointments with available hourly weather in the same grid. Check the selected place and forecast date when planning outdoors.

before: Month view marks every day that has something on it. Year view puts twelve months on one screen — the fastest way to find a free week.
after: Compare selected-calendar events across the month or year. Open a day to inspect all its appointments before deciding that it is free.

before: Tap any hour in the weather hub and a new event opens, already set to that time. Find the dry window, then book it.
after: Choose an available forecast hour to start an event draft, then review its date, time and calendar before saving.

before: Version {v} — shared events now keep themselves up to date
after: Version {v} — sharing for events and calendars

before: Subscriptions are handled by Apple, so you cancel in your App Store account settings. Do it at least 24 hours before the period ends and you will not be charged again.
after: On iPhone or iPad, open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions. Choose Cloud Calendars and cancel there; check the cancellation or expiry status shown by Apple.

before: Subscriptions renew automatically and are billed through your Apple ID. Cancel any time in your App Store account settings, at least 24 hours before the period ends.
after: Subscriptions renew automatically through your Apple Account. Check the local price and billing period before purchase. Manage cancellation in Settings under your name → Subscriptions.
